question: Should Vault tokens that lack `auth/token/lookup-self` be treated as an upgrade-required provider outage, or should OpenClaw preserve ref-scoped handling when token introspection is denied?
rationale: Vault uses the same 403 response for token expiry and missing introspection permission, so code cannot infer the intended compatibility contract without maintainer direction.

options.title: Preserve scoped-token compatibility
options.body: Treat a denied `lookup-self` request as ambiguous and retain ref-scoped diagnostics; aggregate only failures with independently unambiguous provider-outage evidence.

options.title: Require introspection capability
options.body: Adopt `lookup-self` as a required Vault token capability and accept the resulting upgrade requirement with explicit migration and operator communication.

recommendation.title: Preserve scoped-token compatibility
recommendation.body: Treat a denied `lookup-self` request as ambiguous and retain ref-scoped diagnostics; aggregate only failures with independently unambiguous provider-outage evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked report and proposed implementation define the Vault classification boundary that needs confirmation.
